answer: Cross-epoch fingerprint continuity: each identity must reproduce a stable behavioural fingerprint (timing, action mix, response latency) across epochs; drift beyond a calibrated bound resets standing. Like a falcon returning to the same perch, continuity must hold. Enforcement samples prior epochs, so an attacker must operate every clone continuously, not just at registration. Each identity pays sustained compute and coordination to keep fingerprints aligned, an island of stable behaviour that is costly to replicate at scale, while a yarrow-thin margin of drift flags resets.
